questions.stem: Of 30 students, 20 like tea and 15 like coffee. Everyone likes at least one of the two. How many like both?
questions.explain: Adding 20 and 15 gives 35 but there are only 30 students, so 5 were counted twice. Those 5 like both.

questions.stem: Let A = {1, 2, 3, 4}. Which statement is true?
questions.explain: Every element of {1, 2} is in A, so {1, 2} is a subset of A. It is not a member of A, because A has no element that is itself a set.

questions.stem: A relation R is symmetric if for all x and y, xRy implies yRx. Which shows that R is NOT symmetric?
options: Every pair has both xRy and yRx
Some pair has both xRy and yRx
Some pair has xRy but not yRx
questions.explain: Negating “for all x, y: xRy → yRx” gives “for some x, y: xRy and not yRx”. One such pair is enough.

questions.stem: Which statement is the contrapositive of “if p then q”?
options: if not q then not p
if not p then not q
questions.explain: The contrapositive swaps and negates: “if not q then not p”. It always has the same truth value as the original.

questions.stem: For which x is “if x is even then x > 2” false?
questions.explain: An implication is false only when the first part is true and the second is false. x = 2 is even but not greater than 2.
